import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Logic.System
import Foundation.Vorspiel.BinaryRelations
import Foundation.Vorspiel.RelItr

/-
  DEPRECATED!!
-/

universe u v
-- set_option autoImplicit false

namespace LO.Kripke

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

instance : CoeSort Frame (Type u) := ⟨Frame.World⟩
instance : CoeFun Frame (λ F => F.World → F.World → Prop) := ⟨Frame.Rel⟩

instance {F : Frame} : Nonempty F.World := F.World_nonempty

abbrev Frame.Rel' {F : Frame} (x y : F.World) := F.Rel x y
infix:45 " ≺ " => Frame.Rel'

protected abbrev Frame.RelItr' {F : Frame} (n : ℕ) := F.Rel.iterate n
notation x:45 " ≺^[" n "] " y:46 => Frame.RelItr' n x y


noncomputable abbrev Frame.default {F : Frame} : F.World := Classical.choice F.World_nonempty
notation "﹫" => Frame.default


set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev Frame.Dep (α : Type v) := Frame.{u}

abbrev Frame.alt (F : Frame.{u}) (α : Type v) : Frame.Dep α := F
notation F:max "#" α:max => Frame.alt F α


structure FiniteFrame extends Frame where
  [World_finite : Finite World]

instance {F : FiniteFrame} : Finite (F.World) := F.World_finite
instance : Coe (FiniteFrame) (Frame) := ⟨λ F ↦ F.toFrame⟩


abbrev FrameClass := Set (Frame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FrameClass.{u}

abbrev FrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FrameClass) (α : Type v) : FrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass := Set (FiniteFrame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FiniteFrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FiniteFrameClass.{u}

abbrev FiniteFrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) (α : Type v) : FiniteFrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FiniteFrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) : FrameClass := 𝔽.image FiniteFrame.toFrame
-- instance : Coe (FiniteFrameClass) (FrameClass) := ⟨FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass⟩

abbrev FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass (𝔽 : FrameClass) : FiniteFrameClass := { FF | FF.toFrame ∈ 𝔽 }
postfix:max "ꟳ" => FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass


lemma FrameClass.iff_mem_restrictFinite {𝔽 : FrameClass} {F : Frame} (h : F ∈ 𝔽) [Finite F.World] : ⟨F⟩ ∈ 𝔽ꟳ := by simpa;

section

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊` -/
abbrev AllFrameClass : FrameClass := Set.univ

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓` -/
abbrev ReflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐃` -/
abbrev SerialFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Serial F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝟒` -/
abbrev TransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝟓` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/
abbrev ReflexiveEuclideanFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Euclidean F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝐁` -/
abbrev ReflexiveSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Symmetric F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐒𝟓` -/
abbrev UniversalFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Universal F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊.𝟑` -/
abbrev ConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐈𝐧𝐭` and `𝐒𝟒` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F }
alias PreorderFrameClass := ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐂` and `𝐒𝟒.𝟐` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveConfluentFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Confluent F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐋𝐂` and `𝐒𝟒.𝟑` -/

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Logic.System
import Foundation.Vorspiel.BinaryRelations
import Foundation.Vorspiel.RelItr

/-
  DEPRECATED!!
-/

universe u v
-- set_option autoImplicit false

namespace LO.Kripke

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

instance : CoeSort Frame (Type u) := ⟨Frame.World⟩
instance : CoeFun Frame (λ F => F.World → F.World → Prop) := ⟨Frame.Rel⟩

instance {F : Frame} : Nonempty F.World := F.World_nonempty

abbrev Frame.Rel' {F : Frame} (x y : F.World) := F.Rel x y
infix:45 " ≺ " => Frame.Rel'

protected abbrev Frame.RelItr' {F : Frame} (n : ℕ) := F.Rel.iterate n
notation x:45 " ≺^[" n "] " y:46 => Frame.RelItr' n x y


noncomputable abbrev Frame.default {F : Frame} : F.World := Classical.choice F.World_nonempty
notation "﹫" => Frame.default


set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev Frame.Dep (α : Type v) := Frame.{u}

abbrev Frame.alt (F : Frame.{u}) (α : Type v) : Frame.Dep α := F
notation F:max "#" α:max => Frame.alt F α


structure FiniteFrame extends Frame where
  [World_finite : Finite World]

instance {F : FiniteFrame} : Finite (F.World) := F.World_finite
instance : Coe (FiniteFrame) (Frame) := ⟨λ F ↦ F.toFrame⟩


abbrev FrameClass := Set (Frame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FrameClass.{u}

abbrev FrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FrameClass) (α : Type v) : FrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass := Set (FiniteFrame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FiniteFrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FiniteFrameClass.{u}

abbrev FiniteFrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) (α : Type v) : FiniteFrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FiniteFrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) : FrameClass := 𝔽.image FiniteFrame.toFrame
-- instance : Coe (FiniteFrameClass) (FrameClass) := ⟨FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass⟩

abbrev FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass (𝔽 : FrameClass) : FiniteFrameClass := { FF | FF.toFrame ∈ 𝔽 }
postfix:max "ꟳ" => FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass


lemma FrameClass.iff_mem_restrictFinite {𝔽 : FrameClass} {F : Frame} (h : F ∈ 𝔽) [Finite F.World] : ⟨F⟩ ∈ 𝔽ꟳ := by simpa;

section

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊` -/
abbrev AllFrameClass : FrameClass := Set.univ

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓` -/
abbrev ReflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐃` -/
abbrev SerialFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Serial F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝟒` -/
abbrev TransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝟓` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/
abbrev ReflexiveEuclideanFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Euclidean F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝐁` -/
abbrev ReflexiveSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Symmetric F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐒𝟓` -/
abbrev UniversalFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Universal F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊.𝟑` -/
abbrev ConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐈𝐧𝐭` and `𝐒𝟒` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F }
alias PreorderFrameClass := ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐂` and `𝐒𝟒.𝟐` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveConfluentFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Confluent F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐋𝐂` and `𝐒𝟒.𝟑` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐂𝐥` and `𝐊𝐓𝟒𝐁` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Symmetric F }
alias EquivalenceFrameClass := ReflexiveTransitiveSymmetricFrameClass

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐋` -/
abbrev TransitiveConverseWellFoundedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F ∧ ConverseWellFounded F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐋` (Finite version) -/
abbrev TransitiveIrreflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F ∧ Irreflexive F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐫𝐳` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveWeaklyConverseWellFoundedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Transitive F ∧ WeaklyConverseWellFounded F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐫𝐳` (Finite version) -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveAntiSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Transitive F ∧ AntiSymmetric F }

end

  characterize hF := defines.define.mpr hF
  nonempty := defines.nonempty

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Logic.System
import Foundation.Vorspiel.BinaryRelations
import Foundation.Vorspiel.RelItr

/-
  DEPRECATED!!
-/

universe u v
-- set_option autoImplicit false

namespace LO.Kripke

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

instance : CoeSort Frame (Type u) := ⟨Frame.World⟩
instance : CoeFun Frame (λ F => F.World → F.World → Prop) := ⟨Frame.Rel⟩

instance {F : Frame} : Nonempty F.World := F.World_nonempty

abbrev Frame.Rel' {F : Frame} (x y : F.World) := F.Rel x y
infix:45 " ≺ " => Frame.Rel'

protected abbrev Frame.RelItr' {F : Frame} (n : ℕ) := F.Rel.iterate n
notation x:45 " ≺^[" n "] " y:46 => Frame.RelItr' n x y


noncomputable abbrev Frame.default {F : Frame} : F.World := Classical.choice F.World_nonempty
notation "﹫" => Frame.default


set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev Frame.Dep (α : Type v) := Frame.{u}

abbrev Frame.alt (F : Frame.{u}) (α : Type v) : Frame.Dep α := F
notation F:max "#" α:max => Frame.alt F α


structure FiniteFrame extends Frame where
  [World_finite : Finite World]

instance {F : FiniteFrame} : Finite (F.World) := F.World_finite
instance : Coe (FiniteFrame) (Frame) := ⟨λ F ↦ F.toFrame⟩


abbrev FrameClass := Set (Frame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FrameClass.{u}

abbrev FrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FrameClass) (α : Type v) : FrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass := Set (FiniteFrame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FiniteFrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FiniteFrameClass.{u}

abbrev FiniteFrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) (α : Type v) : FiniteFrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FiniteFrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) : FrameClass := 𝔽.image FiniteFrame.toFrame
-- instance : Coe (FiniteFrameClass) (FrameClass) := ⟨FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass⟩

abbrev FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass (𝔽 : FrameClass) : FiniteFrameClass := { FF | FF.toFrame ∈ 𝔽 }
postfix:max "ꟳ" => FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass


lemma FrameClass.iff_mem_restrictFinite {𝔽 : FrameClass} {F : Frame} (h : F ∈ 𝔽) [Finite F.World] : ⟨F⟩ ∈ 𝔽ꟳ := by simpa;

section

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊` -/
abbrev AllFrameClass : FrameClass := Set.univ

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓` -/
abbrev ReflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐃` -/
abbrev SerialFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Serial F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝟒` -/
abbrev TransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝟓` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/
abbrev ReflexiveEuclideanFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Euclidean F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝐁` -/
abbrev ReflexiveSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Symmetric F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐒𝟓` -/
abbrev UniversalFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Universal F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊.𝟑` -/
abbrev ConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐈𝐧𝐭` and `𝐒𝟒` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F }
alias PreorderFrameClass := ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐂` and `𝐒𝟒.𝟐` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveConfluentFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Confluent F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐋𝐂` and `𝐒𝟒.𝟑` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐂𝐥` and `𝐊𝐓𝟒𝐁` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Symmetric F }
alias EquivalenceFrameClass := ReflexiveTransitiveSymmetricFrameClass

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐋` -/
abbrev TransitiveConverseWellFoundedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F ∧ ConverseWellFounded F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐋` (Finite version) -/
abbrev TransitiveIrreflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F ∧ Irreflexive F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐫𝐳` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveWeaklyConverseWellFoundedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Transitive F ∧ WeaklyConverseWellFounded F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐫𝐳` (Finite version) -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveAntiSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Transitive F ∧ AntiSymmetric F }

end

class FrameClass.Characteraizable (𝔽₁ : FrameClass) (𝔽₂ : outParam (FrameClass)) where
  characterize : ∀ {F}, F ∈ 𝔽₂ → F ∈ 𝔽₁
  nonempty : 𝔽₂.Nonempty

/-- `𝔽₁` is defined by `𝔽₂` -/
class FrameClass.DefinedBy (𝔽₁ : FrameClass) (𝔽₂ : outParam (FrameClass)) where
  define : ∀ {F}, F ∈ 𝔽₁ ↔ F ∈ 𝔽₂
  nonempty : 𝔽₂.Nonempty

instance {𝔽₁ 𝔽₂ : FrameClass} [defines : 𝔽₁.DefinedBy 𝔽₂] : FrameClass.Characteraizable 𝔽₁ 𝔽₂ where
  characterize hF := defines.define.mpr hF
  nonempty := defines.nonempty

  nonempty : 𝔽₂.Nonempty

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Logic.System
import Foundation.Vorspiel.BinaryRelations
import Foundation.Vorspiel.RelItr

/-

universe u v
-- set_option autoImplicit false

namespace LO.Kripke

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

instance : CoeSort Frame (Type u) := ⟨Frame.World⟩
instance : CoeFun Frame (λ F => F.World → F.World → Prop) := ⟨Frame.Rel⟩

instance {F : Frame} : Nonempty F.World := F.World_nonempty

abbrev Frame.Rel' {F : Frame} (x y : F.World) := F.Rel x y
infix:45 " ≺ " => Frame.Rel'

protected abbrev Frame.RelItr' {F : Frame} (n : ℕ) := F.Rel.iterate n
notation x:45 " ≺^[" n "] " y:46 => Frame.RelItr' n x y


noncomputable abbrev Frame.default {F : Frame} : F.World := Classical.choice F.World_nonempty
notation "﹫" => Frame.default


set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev Frame.Dep (α : Type v) := Frame.{u}

abbrev Frame.alt (F : Frame.{u}) (α : Type v) : Frame.Dep α := F
notation F:max "#" α:max => Frame.alt F α


structure FiniteFrame extends Frame where
  [World_finite : Finite World]

instance {F : FiniteFrame} : Finite (F.World) := F.World_finite
instance : Coe (FiniteFrame) (Frame) := ⟨λ F ↦ F.toFrame⟩


abbrev FrameClass := Set (Frame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in

postfix:max "ꟳ" => FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass


lemma FrameClass.iff_mem_restrictFinite {𝔽 : FrameClass} {F : Frame} (h : F ∈ 𝔽) [Finite F.World] : ⟨F⟩ ∈ 𝔽ꟳ := by simpa;

section

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊` -/
abbrev AllFrameClass : FrameClass := Set.univ

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓` -/
abbrev ReflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐃` -/
abbrev SerialFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Serial F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝟒` -/
abbrev TransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝟓` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/
abbrev ReflexiveEuclideanFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Euclidean F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝐁` -/
abbrev ReflexiveSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Symmetric F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐒𝟓` -/
abbrev UniversalFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Universal F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊.𝟑` -/
abbrev ConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐈𝐧𝐭` and `𝐒𝟒` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F }
alias PreorderFrameClass := ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐂` and `𝐒𝟒.𝟐` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveConfluentFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Confluent F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐋𝐂` and `𝐒𝟒.𝟑` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐂𝐥` and `𝐊𝐓𝟒𝐁` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Symmetric F }
alias EquivalenceFrameClass := ReflexiveTransitiveSymmetricFrameClass

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐋` -/
abbrev TransitiveConverseWellFoundedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F ∧ ConverseWellFounded F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐋` (Finite version) -/
abbrev TransitiveIrreflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F ∧ Irreflexive F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐫𝐳` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveWeaklyConverseWellFoundedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Transitive F ∧ WeaklyConverseWellFounded F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐫𝐳` (Finite version) -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveAntiSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Transitive F ∧ AntiSymmetric F }

end

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Logic.System
import Foundation.Vorspiel.BinaryRelations
import Foundation.Vorspiel.RelItr

/-
  DEPRECATED!!
-/

universe u v
-- set_option autoImplicit false

namespace LO.Kripke

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Logic.System
import Foundation.Vorspiel.BinaryRelations
import Foundation.Vorspiel.RelItr

/-
  DEPRECATED!!
-/

universe u v
-- set_option autoImplicit false

namespace LO.Kripke

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

instance : CoeSort Frame (Type u) := ⟨Frame.World⟩
instance : CoeFun Frame (λ F => F.World → F.World → Prop) := ⟨Frame.Rel⟩

instance {F : Frame} : Nonempty F.World := F.World_nonempty

abbrev Frame.Rel' {F : Frame} (x y : F.World) := F.Rel x y
infix:45 " ≺ " => Frame.Rel'

protected abbrev Frame.RelItr' {F : Frame} (n : ℕ) := F.Rel.iterate n
notation x:45 " ≺^[" n "] " y:46 => Frame.RelItr' n x y


noncomputable abbrev Frame.default {F : Frame} : F.World := Classical.choice F.World_nonempty
notation "﹫" => Frame.default


set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev Frame.Dep (α : Type v) := Frame.{u}

abbrev Frame.alt (F : Frame.{u}) (α : Type v) : Frame.Dep α := F
notation F:max "#" α:max => Frame.alt F α


structure FiniteFrame extends Frame where
  [World_finite : Finite World]

instance {F : FiniteFrame} : Finite (F.World) := F.World_finite
instance : Coe (FiniteFrame) (Frame) := ⟨λ F ↦ F.toFrame⟩


abbrev FrameClass := Set (Frame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FrameClass.{u}

abbrev FrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FrameClass) (α : Type v) : FrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass := Set (FiniteFrame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FiniteFrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FiniteFrameClass.{u}

abbrev FiniteFrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) (α : Type v) : FiniteFrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FiniteFrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) : FrameClass := 𝔽.image FiniteFrame.toFrame
-- instance : Coe (FiniteFrameClass) (FrameClass) := ⟨FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass⟩

abbrev FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass (𝔽 : FrameClass) : FiniteFrameClass := { FF | FF.toFrame ∈ 𝔽 }
postfix:max "ꟳ" => FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass


lemma FrameClass.iff_mem_restrictFinite {𝔽 : FrameClass} {F : Frame} (h : F ∈ 𝔽) [Finite F.World] : ⟨F⟩ ∈ 𝔽ꟳ := by simpa;

abbrev UniversalFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Universal F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊.𝟑` -/

import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Logic.System
import Foundation.Vorspiel.BinaryRelations
import Foundation.Vorspiel.RelItr

/-
  DEPRECATED!!
-/

universe u v
-- set_option autoImplicit false

namespace LO.Kripke

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

instance : CoeSort Frame (Type u) := ⟨Frame.World⟩
instance : CoeFun Frame (λ F => F.World → F.World → Prop) := ⟨Frame.Rel⟩

instance {F : Frame} : Nonempty F.World := F.World_nonempty

abbrev Frame.Rel' {F : Frame} (x y : F.World) := F.Rel x y
infix:45 " ≺ " => Frame.Rel'

protected abbrev Frame.RelItr' {F : Frame} (n : ℕ) := F.Rel.iterate n
notation x:45 " ≺^[" n "] " y:46 => Frame.RelItr' n x y


noncomputable abbrev Frame.default {F : Frame} : F.World := Classical.choice F.World_nonempty
notation "﹫" => Frame.default


set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev Frame.Dep (α : Type v) := Frame.{u}

abbrev Frame.alt (F : Frame.{u}) (α : Type v) : Frame.Dep α := F
notation F:max "#" α:max => Frame.alt F α


structure FiniteFrame extends Frame where
  [World_finite : Finite World]

instance {F : FiniteFrame} : Finite (F.World) := F.World_finite
instance : Coe (FiniteFrame) (Frame) := ⟨λ F ↦ F.toFrame⟩


abbrev FrameClass := Set (Frame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FrameClass.{u}

abbrev FrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FrameClass) (α : Type v) : FrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass := Set (FiniteFrame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FiniteFrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FiniteFrameClass.{u}

abbrev FiniteFrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) (α : Type v) : FiniteFrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FiniteFrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) : FrameClass := 𝔽.image FiniteFrame.toFrame
-- instance : Coe (FiniteFrameClass) (FrameClass) := ⟨FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass⟩

abbrev FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass (𝔽 : FrameClass) : FiniteFrameClass := { FF | FF.toFrame ∈ 𝔽 }
postfix:max "ꟳ" => FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass


lemma FrameClass.iff_mem_restrictFinite {𝔽 : FrameClass} {F : Frame} (h : F ∈ 𝔽) [Finite F.World] : ⟨F⟩ ∈ 𝔽ꟳ := by simpa;

section

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊` -/
abbrev AllFrameClass : FrameClass := Set.univ

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓` -/
abbrev ReflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐃` -/
abbrev SerialFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Serial F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝟒` -/
abbrev TransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝟓` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/
abbrev ReflexiveEuclideanFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Euclidean F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝐁` -/
abbrev ReflexiveSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Symmetric F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐒𝟓` -/
abbrev UniversalFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Universal F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊.𝟑` -/
abbrev ConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐈𝐧𝐭` and `𝐒𝟒` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F }
alias PreorderFrameClass := ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐂` and `𝐒𝟒.𝟐` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveConfluentFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Confluent F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐋𝐂` and `𝐒𝟒.𝟑` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐂𝐥` and `𝐊𝐓𝟒𝐁` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Symmetric F }
alias EquivalenceFrameClass := ReflexiveTransitiveSymmetricFrameClass

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐋` -/
abbrev TransitiveConverseWellFoundedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F ∧ ConverseWellFounded F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐋` (Finite version) -/
abbrev TransitiveIrreflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F ∧ Irreflexive F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐫𝐳` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveWeaklyConverseWellFoundedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Transitive F ∧ WeaklyConverseWellFounded F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐫𝐳` (Finite version) -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveAntiSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Transitive F ∧ AntiSymmetric F }

end

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Logic.System
import Foundation.Vorspiel.BinaryRelations
import Foundation.Vorspiel.RelItr

/-
  DEPRECATED!!
-/

universe u v
-- set_option autoImplicit false

namespace LO.Kripke

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

instance : CoeSort Frame (Type u) := ⟨Frame.World⟩
instance : CoeFun Frame (λ F => F.World → F.World → Prop) := ⟨Frame.Rel⟩

instance {F : Frame} : Nonempty F.World := F.World_nonempty

abbrev Frame.Rel' {F : Frame} (x y : F.World) := F.Rel x y
infix:45 " ≺ " => Frame.Rel'

protected abbrev Frame.RelItr' {F : Frame} (n : ℕ) := F.Rel.iterate n
notation x:45 " ≺^[" n "] " y:46 => Frame.RelItr' n x y


noncomputable abbrev Frame.default {F : Frame} : F.World := Classical.choice F.World_nonempty
notation "﹫" => Frame.default


set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev Frame.Dep (α : Type v) := Frame.{u}

abbrev Frame.alt (F : Frame.{u}) (α : Type v) : Frame.Dep α := F
notation F:max "#" α:max => Frame.alt F α


structure FiniteFrame extends Frame where
  [World_finite : Finite World]

instance {F : FiniteFrame} : Finite (F.World) := F.World_finite
instance : Coe (FiniteFrame) (Frame) := ⟨λ F ↦ F.toFrame⟩


abbrev FrameClass := Set (Frame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FrameClass.{u}

abbrev FrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FrameClass) (α : Type v) : FrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass := Set (FiniteFrame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FiniteFrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FiniteFrameClass.{u}

abbrev FiniteFrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) (α : Type v) : FiniteFrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FiniteFrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) : FrameClass := 𝔽.image FiniteFrame.toFrame
-- instance : Coe (FiniteFrameClass) (FrameClass) := ⟨FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass⟩

abbrev FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass (𝔽 : FrameClass) : FiniteFrameClass := { FF | FF.toFrame ∈ 𝔽 }
postfix:max "ꟳ" => FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass


lemma FrameClass.iff_mem_restrictFinite {𝔽 : FrameClass} {F : Frame} (h : F ∈ 𝔽) [Finite F.World] : ⟨F⟩ ∈ 𝔽ꟳ := by simpa;

section

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊` -/
abbrev AllFrameClass : FrameClass := Set.univ

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓` -/
abbrev ReflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐃` -/
abbrev SerialFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Serial F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝟒` -/
abbrev TransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝟓` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/
abbrev ReflexiveEuclideanFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Euclidean F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝐁` -/
abbrev ReflexiveSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Symmetric F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐒𝟓` -/
abbrev UniversalFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Universal F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊.𝟑` -/
abbrev ConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐈𝐧𝐭` and `𝐒𝟒` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F }
alias PreorderFrameClass := ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐂` and `𝐒𝟒.𝟐` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveConfluentFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Confluent F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐋𝐂` and `𝐒𝟒.𝟑` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐂𝐥` and `𝐊𝐓𝟒𝐁` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Symmetric F }
alias EquivalenceFrameClass := ReflexiveTransitiveSymmetricFrameClass

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐋` -/
abbrev TransitiveConverseWellFoundedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F ∧ ConverseWellFounded F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐋` (Finite version) -/
abbrev TransitiveIrreflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F ∧ Irreflexive F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐫𝐳` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveWeaklyConverseWellFoundedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Transitive F ∧ WeaklyConverseWellFounded F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐫𝐳` (Finite version) -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveAntiSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Transitive F ∧ AntiSymmetric F }

end

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Logic.System
import Foundation.Vorspiel.BinaryRelations
import Foundation.Vorspiel.RelItr

/-
  DEPRECATED!!
-/

universe u v
-- set_option autoImplicit false

namespace LO.Kripke

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

instance : CoeSort Frame (Type u) := ⟨Frame.World⟩
instance : CoeFun Frame (λ F => F.World → F.World → Prop) := ⟨Frame.Rel⟩

instance {F : Frame} : Nonempty F.World := F.World_nonempty

abbrev Frame.Rel' {F : Frame} (x y : F.World) := F.Rel x y
infix:45 " ≺ " => Frame.Rel'

protected abbrev Frame.RelItr' {F : Frame} (n : ℕ) := F.Rel.iterate n
notation x:45 " ≺^[" n "] " y:46 => Frame.RelItr' n x y


noncomputable abbrev Frame.default {F : Frame} : F.World := Classical.choice F.World_nonempty
notation "﹫" => Frame.default


set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev Frame.Dep (α : Type v) := Frame.{u}

abbrev Frame.alt (F : Frame.{u}) (α : Type v) : Frame.Dep α := F
notation F:max "#" α:max => Frame.alt F α


structure FiniteFrame extends Frame where
  [World_finite : Finite World]

instance {F : FiniteFrame} : Finite (F.World) := F.World_finite
instance : Coe (FiniteFrame) (Frame) := ⟨λ F ↦ F.toFrame⟩


abbrev FrameClass := Set (Frame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FrameClass.{u}

abbrev FrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FrameClass) (α : Type v) : FrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass := Set (FiniteFrame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FiniteFrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FiniteFrameClass.{u}

abbrev FiniteFrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) (α : Type v) : FiniteFrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FiniteFrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) : FrameClass := 𝔽.image FiniteFrame.toFrame
-- instance : Coe (FiniteFrameClass) (FrameClass) := ⟨FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass⟩

abbrev FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass (𝔽 : FrameClass) : FiniteFrameClass := { FF | FF.toFrame ∈ 𝔽 }
postfix:max "ꟳ" => FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass


lemma FrameClass.iff_mem_restrictFinite {𝔽 : FrameClass} {F : Frame} (h : F ∈ 𝔽) [Finite F.World] : ⟨F⟩ ∈ 𝔽ꟳ := by simpa;

section

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊` -/
abbrev AllFrameClass : FrameClass := Set.univ

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓` -/
abbrev ReflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐃` -/
abbrev SerialFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Serial F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝟒` -/
abbrev TransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝟓` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/
abbrev ReflexiveEuclideanFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Euclidean F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝐁` -/
abbrev ReflexiveSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Symmetric F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐒𝟓` -/
abbrev UniversalFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Universal F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊.𝟑` -/
abbrev ConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐈𝐧𝐭` and `𝐒𝟒` -/

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Logic.System
import Foundation.Vorspiel.BinaryRelations
import Foundation.Vorspiel.RelItr

/-
  DEPRECATED!!
-/

universe u v
-- set_option autoImplicit false

namespace LO.Kripke

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

instance : CoeSort Frame (Type u) := ⟨Frame.World⟩
instance : CoeFun Frame (λ F => F.World → F.World → Prop) := ⟨Frame.Rel⟩

instance {F : Frame} : Nonempty F.World := F.World_nonempty

abbrev Frame.Rel' {F : Frame} (x y : F.World) := F.Rel x y
infix:45 " ≺ " => Frame.Rel'

protected abbrev Frame.RelItr' {F : Frame} (n : ℕ) := F.Rel.iterate n
notation x:45 " ≺^[" n "] " y:46 => Frame.RelItr' n x y


noncomputable abbrev Frame.default {F : Frame} : F.World := Classical.choice F.World_nonempty
notation "﹫" => Frame.default


set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev Frame.Dep (α : Type v) := Frame.{u}

abbrev Frame.alt (F : Frame.{u}) (α : Type v) : Frame.Dep α := F
notation F:max "#" α:max => Frame.alt F α


structure FiniteFrame extends Frame where
  [World_finite : Finite World]

instance {F : FiniteFrame} : Finite (F.World) := F.World_finite
instance : Coe (FiniteFrame) (Frame) := ⟨λ F ↦ F.toFrame⟩


abbrev FrameClass := Set (Frame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FrameClass.{u}

abbrev FrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FrameClass) (α : Type v) : FrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass := Set (FiniteFrame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FiniteFrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FiniteFrameClass.{u}

abbrev FiniteFrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) (α : Type v) : FiniteFrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FiniteFrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) : FrameClass := 𝔽.image FiniteFrame.toFrame
-- instance : Coe (FiniteFrameClass) (FrameClass) := ⟨FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass⟩

abbrev FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass (𝔽 : FrameClass) : FiniteFrameClass := { FF | FF.toFrame ∈ 𝔽 }
postfix:max "ꟳ" => FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass


lemma FrameClass.iff_mem_restrictFinite {𝔽 : FrameClass} {F : Frame} (h : F ∈ 𝔽) [Finite F.World] : ⟨F⟩ ∈ 𝔽ꟳ := by simpa;

section

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊` -/
abbrev AllFrameClass : FrameClass := Set.univ

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓` -/
abbrev ReflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐃` -/
abbrev SerialFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Serial F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝟒` -/
abbrev TransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝟓` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/
abbrev ReflexiveEuclideanFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Euclidean F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝐁` -/
abbrev ReflexiveSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Symmetric F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐒𝟓` -/
abbrev UniversalFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Universal F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊.𝟑` -/
abbrev ConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐈𝐧𝐭` and `𝐒𝟒` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F }
alias PreorderFrameClass := ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐂` and `𝐒𝟒.𝟐` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveConfluentFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Confluent F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐋𝐂` and `𝐒𝟒.𝟑` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐂𝐥` and `𝐊𝐓𝟒𝐁` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Symmetric F }
alias EquivalenceFrameClass := ReflexiveTransitiveSymmetricFrameClass

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐋` -/
abbrev TransitiveConverseWellFoundedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F ∧ ConverseWellFounded F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐋` (Finite version) -/
abbrev TransitiveIrreflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F ∧ Irreflexive F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐫𝐳` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveWeaklyConverseWellFoundedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Transitive F ∧ WeaklyConverseWellFounded F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐫𝐳` (Finite version) -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveAntiSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Transitive F ∧ AntiSymmetric F }

end

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Logic.System
import Foundation.Vorspiel.BinaryRelations
import Foundation.Vorspiel.RelItr

/-
  DEPRECATED!!
-/

universe u v
-- set_option autoImplicit false

namespace LO.Kripke

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

instance : CoeSort Frame (Type u) := ⟨Frame.World⟩
instance : CoeFun Frame (λ F => F.World → F.World → Prop) := ⟨Frame.Rel⟩

instance {F : Frame} : Nonempty F.World := F.World_nonempty

abbrev Frame.Rel' {F : Frame} (x y : F.World) := F.Rel x y
infix:45 " ≺ " => Frame.Rel'

protected abbrev Frame.RelItr' {F : Frame} (n : ℕ) := F.Rel.iterate n
notation x:45 " ≺^[" n "] " y:46 => Frame.RelItr' n x y


noncomputable abbrev Frame.default {F : Frame} : F.World := Classical.choice F.World_nonempty
notation "﹫" => Frame.default

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Logic.System
import Foundation.Vorspiel.BinaryRelations
import Foundation.Vorspiel.RelItr

/-
  DEPRECATED!!
-/

universe u v
-- set_option autoImplicit false

namespace LO.Kripke

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

instance : CoeSort Frame (Type u) := ⟨Frame.World⟩
instance : CoeFun Frame (λ F => F.World → F.World → Prop) := ⟨Frame.Rel⟩

instance {F : Frame} : Nonempty F.World := F.World_nonempty

abbrev Frame.Rel' {F : Frame} (x y : F.World) := F.Rel x y
infix:45 " ≺ " => Frame.Rel'

protected abbrev Frame.RelItr' {F : Frame} (n : ℕ) := F.Rel.iterate n
notation x:45 " ≺^[" n "] " y:46 => Frame.RelItr' n x y


noncomputable abbrev Frame.default {F : Frame} : F.World := Classical.choice F.World_nonempty
notation "﹫" => Frame.default


set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev Frame.Dep (α : Type v) := Frame.{u}

abbrev Frame.alt (F : Frame.{u}) (α : Type v) : Frame.Dep α := F
notation F:max "#" α:max => Frame.alt F α


structure FiniteFrame extends Frame where
  [World_finite : Finite World]

instance {F : FiniteFrame} : Finite (F.World) := F.World_finite
instance : Coe (FiniteFrame) (Frame) := ⟨λ F ↦ F.toFrame⟩


abbrev FrameClass := Set (Frame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FrameClass.{u}

abbrev FrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FrameClass) (α : Type v) : FrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass := Set (FiniteFrame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FiniteFrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FiniteFrameClass.{u}

abbrev FiniteFrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) (α : Type v) : FiniteFrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FiniteFrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) : FrameClass := 𝔽.image FiniteFrame.toFrame
-- instance : Coe (FiniteFrameClass) (FrameClass) := ⟨FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass⟩

abbrev FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass (𝔽 : FrameClass) : FiniteFrameClass := { FF | FF.toFrame ∈ 𝔽 }
postfix:max "ꟳ" => FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass


lemma FrameClass.iff_mem_restrictFinite {𝔽 : FrameClass} {F : Frame} (h : F ∈ 𝔽) [Finite F.World] : ⟨F⟩ ∈ 𝔽ꟳ := by simpa;

section

abbrev ReflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐋` -/

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Logic.System
import Foundation.Vorspiel.BinaryRelations
import Foundation.Vorspiel.RelItr

/-
  DEPRECATED!!
-/

universe u v
-- set_option autoImplicit false

namespace LO.Kripke

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

instance : CoeSort Frame (Type u) := ⟨Frame.World⟩
instance : CoeFun Frame (λ F => F.World → F.World → Prop) := ⟨Frame.Rel⟩

instance {F : Frame} : Nonempty F.World := F.World_nonempty

abbrev Frame.Rel' {F : Frame} (x y : F.World) := F.Rel x y
infix:45 " ≺ " => Frame.Rel'

protected abbrev Frame.RelItr' {F : Frame} (n : ℕ) := F.Rel.iterate n
notation x:45 " ≺^[" n "] " y:46 => Frame.RelItr' n x y


noncomputable abbrev Frame.default {F : Frame} : F.World := Classical.choice F.World_nonempty
notation "﹫" => Frame.default

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Logic.System
import Foundation.Vorspiel.BinaryRelations
import Foundation.Vorspiel.RelItr

/-
  DEPRECATED!!
-/

universe u v
-- set_option autoImplicit false

namespace LO.Kripke

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

instance : CoeSort Frame (Type u) := ⟨Frame.World⟩
instance : CoeFun Frame (λ F => F.World → F.World → Prop) := ⟨Frame.Rel⟩

instance {F : Frame} : Nonempty F.World := F.World_nonempty

abbrev Frame.Rel' {F : Frame} (x y : F.World) := F.Rel x y
infix:45 " ≺ " => Frame.Rel'

protected abbrev Frame.RelItr' {F : Frame} (n : ℕ) := F.Rel.iterate n
notation x:45 " ≺^[" n "] " y:46 => Frame.RelItr' n x y


noncomputable abbrev Frame.default {F : Frame} : F.World := Classical.choice F.World_nonempty
notation "﹫" => Frame.default


set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev Frame.Dep (α : Type v) := Frame.{u}

abbrev Frame.alt (F : Frame.{u}) (α : Type v) : Frame.Dep α := F
notation F:max "#" α:max => Frame.alt F α


structure FiniteFrame extends Frame where
  [World_finite : Finite World]

instance {F : FiniteFrame} : Finite (F.World) := F.World_finite
instance : Coe (FiniteFrame) (Frame) := ⟨λ F ↦ F.toFrame⟩


abbrev FrameClass := Set (Frame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in

notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass := Set (FiniteFrame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FiniteFrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FiniteFrameClass.{u}

abbrev FiniteFrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) (α : Type v) : FiniteFrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FiniteFrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) : FrameClass := 𝔽.image FiniteFrame.toFrame
-- instance : Coe (FiniteFrameClass) (FrameClass) := ⟨FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass⟩

abbrev FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass (𝔽 : FrameClass) : FiniteFrameClass := { FF | FF.toFrame ∈ 𝔽 }
postfix:max "ꟳ" => FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass


lemma FrameClass.iff_mem_restrictFinite {𝔽 : FrameClass} {F : Frame} (h : F ∈ 𝔽) [Finite F.World] : ⟨F⟩ ∈ 𝔽ꟳ := by simpa;

section

abbrev AllFrameClass : FrameClass := Set.univ

abbrev ReflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel }

abbrev ReflexiveSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Symmetric F }

abbrev UniversalFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Universal F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊.𝟑` -/
abbrev ConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐈𝐧𝐭` and `𝐒𝟒` -/

alias PreorderFrameClass := ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass

/-- FrameClass for `𝐂𝐥` and `𝐊𝐓𝟒𝐁` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/

alias EquivalenceFrameClass := ReflexiveTransitiveSymmetricFrameClass

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Logic.System
import Foundation.Vorspiel.BinaryRelations
import Foundation.Vorspiel.RelItr

/-
  DEPRECATED!!
-/

universe u v
-- set_option autoImplicit false

namespace LO.Kripke

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

instance : CoeSort Frame (Type u) := ⟨Frame.World⟩
instance : CoeFun Frame (λ F => F.World → F.World → Prop) := ⟨Frame.Rel⟩

instance {F : Frame} : Nonempty F.World := F.World_nonempty

abbrev Frame.Rel' {F : Frame} (x y : F.World) := F.Rel x y
infix:45 " ≺ " => Frame.Rel'

protected abbrev Frame.RelItr' {F : Frame} (n : ℕ) := F.Rel.iterate n
notation x:45 " ≺^[" n "] " y:46 => Frame.RelItr' n x y


noncomputable abbrev Frame.default {F : Frame} : F.World := Classical.choice F.World_nonempty
notation "﹫" => Frame.default


set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev Frame.Dep (α : Type v) := Frame.{u}

abbrev Frame.alt (F : Frame.{u}) (α : Type v) : Frame.Dep α := F
notation F:max "#" α:max => Frame.alt F α


structure FiniteFrame extends Frame where
  [World_finite : Finite World]

instance {F : FiniteFrame} : Finite (F.World) := F.World_finite
instance : Coe (FiniteFrame) (Frame) := ⟨λ F ↦ F.toFrame⟩


abbrev FrameClass := Set (Frame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FrameClass.{u}

abbrev FrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FrameClass) (α : Type v) : FrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass := Set (FiniteFrame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FiniteFrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FiniteFrameClass.{u}

abbrev FiniteFrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) (α : Type v) : FiniteFrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FiniteFrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) : FrameClass := 𝔽.image FiniteFrame.toFrame
-- instance : Coe (FiniteFrameClass) (FrameClass) := ⟨FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass⟩

abbrev FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass (𝔽 : FrameClass) : FiniteFrameClass := { FF | FF.toFrame ∈ 𝔽 }
postfix:max "ꟳ" => FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass


lemma FrameClass.iff_mem_restrictFinite {𝔽 : FrameClass} {F : Frame} (h : F ∈ 𝔽) [Finite F.World] : ⟨F⟩ ∈ 𝔽ꟳ := by simpa;

section

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊` -/
abbrev AllFrameClass : FrameClass := Set.univ

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓` -/
abbrev ReflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐃` -/
abbrev SerialFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Serial F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝟒` -/
abbrev TransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝟓` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/
abbrev ReflexiveEuclideanFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Euclidean F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝐁` -/
abbrev ReflexiveSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Symmetric F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐒𝟓` -/
abbrev UniversalFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Universal F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊.𝟑` -/
abbrev ConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐈𝐧𝐭` and `𝐒𝟒` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F }
alias PreorderFrameClass := ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐂` and `𝐒𝟒.𝟐` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveConfluentFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Confluent F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐋𝐂` and `𝐒𝟒.𝟑` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐂𝐥` and `𝐊𝐓𝟒𝐁` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Logic.System
import Foundation.Vorspiel.BinaryRelations
import Foundation.Vorspiel.RelItr

/-
  DEPRECATED!!
-/

universe u v
-- set_option autoImplicit false

namespace LO.Kripke

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

instance : CoeSort Frame (Type u) := ⟨Frame.World⟩
instance : CoeFun Frame (λ F => F.World → F.World → Prop) := ⟨Frame.Rel⟩

instance {F : Frame} : Nonempty F.World := F.World_nonempty

abbrev Frame.Rel' {F : Frame} (x y : F.World) := F.Rel x y
infix:45 " ≺ " => Frame.Rel'

protected abbrev Frame.RelItr' {F : Frame} (n : ℕ) := F.Rel.iterate n
notation x:45 " ≺^[" n "] " y:46 => Frame.RelItr' n x y


noncomputable abbrev Frame.default {F : Frame} : F.World := Classical.choice F.World_nonempty
notation "﹫" => Frame.default


set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev Frame.Dep (α : Type v) := Frame.{u}

abbrev Frame.alt (F : Frame.{u}) (α : Type v) : Frame.Dep α := F
notation F:max "#" α:max => Frame.alt F α


structure FiniteFrame extends Frame where
  [World_finite : Finite World]

instance {F : FiniteFrame} : Finite (F.World) := F.World_finite
instance : Coe (FiniteFrame) (Frame) := ⟨λ F ↦ F.toFrame⟩


abbrev FrameClass := Set (Frame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FrameClass.{u}

abbrev FrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FrameClass) (α : Type v) : FrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass := Set (FiniteFrame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FiniteFrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FiniteFrameClass.{u}

abbrev FiniteFrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) (α : Type v) : FiniteFrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FiniteFrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) : FrameClass := 𝔽.image FiniteFrame.toFrame
-- instance : Coe (FiniteFrameClass) (FrameClass) := ⟨FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass⟩

abbrev FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass (𝔽 : FrameClass) : FiniteFrameClass := { FF | FF.toFrame ∈ 𝔽 }
postfix:max "ꟳ" => FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass


lemma FrameClass.iff_mem_restrictFinite {𝔽 : FrameClass} {F : Frame} (h : F ∈ 𝔽) [Finite F.World] : ⟨F⟩ ∈ 𝔽ꟳ := by simpa;

section

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊` -/
abbrev AllFrameClass : FrameClass := Set.univ

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓` -/
abbrev ReflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐃` -/
abbrev SerialFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Serial F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝟒` -/
abbrev TransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝟓` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/
abbrev ReflexiveEuclideanFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Euclidean F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝐁` -/
abbrev ReflexiveSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Symmetric F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐒𝟓` -/
abbrev UniversalFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Universal F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊.𝟑` -/
abbrev ConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐈𝐧𝐭` and `𝐒𝟒` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F }
alias PreorderFrameClass := ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐂` and `𝐒𝟒.𝟐` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveConfluentFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Confluent F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐋𝐂` and `𝐒𝟒.𝟑` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐂𝐥` and `𝐊𝐓𝟒𝐁` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Symmetric F }
alias EquivalenceFrameClass := ReflexiveTransitiveSymmetricFrameClass

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐋` -/
abbrev TransitiveConverseWellFoundedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F ∧ ConverseWellFounded F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐋` (Finite version) -/
abbrev TransitiveIrreflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F ∧ Irreflexive F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐫𝐳` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveWeaklyConverseWellFoundedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Transitive F ∧ WeaklyConverseWellFounded F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐫𝐳` (Finite version) -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveAntiSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Transitive F ∧ AntiSymmetric F }

end

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Logic.System
import Foundation.Vorspiel.BinaryRelations
import Foundation.Vorspiel.RelItr

/-
  DEPRECATED!!
-/

universe u v
-- set_option autoImplicit false

namespace LO.Kripke

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

instance : CoeSort Frame (Type u) := ⟨Frame.World⟩
instance : CoeFun Frame (λ F => F.World → F.World → Prop) := ⟨Frame.Rel⟩

instance {F : Frame} : Nonempty F.World := F.World_nonempty

abbrev Frame.Rel' {F : Frame} (x y : F.World) := F.Rel x y
infix:45 " ≺ " => Frame.Rel'

protected abbrev Frame.RelItr' {F : Frame} (n : ℕ) := F.Rel.iterate n
notation x:45 " ≺^[" n "] " y:46 => Frame.RelItr' n x y


noncomputable abbrev Frame.default {F : Frame} : F.World := Classical.choice F.World_nonempty
notation "﹫" => Frame.default


set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev Frame.Dep (α : Type v) := Frame.{u}

abbrev Frame.alt (F : Frame.{u}) (α : Type v) : Frame.Dep α := F
notation F:max "#" α:max => Frame.alt F α


structure FiniteFrame extends Frame where
  [World_finite : Finite World]

instance {F : FiniteFrame} : Finite (F.World) := F.World_finite
instance : Coe (FiniteFrame) (Frame) := ⟨λ F ↦ F.toFrame⟩


abbrev FrameClass := Set (Frame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FrameClass.{u}

abbrev FrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FrameClass) (α : Type v) : FrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass := Set (FiniteFrame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FiniteFrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FiniteFrameClass.{u}

abbrev FiniteFrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) (α : Type v) : FiniteFrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FiniteFrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) : FrameClass := 𝔽.image FiniteFrame.toFrame
-- instance : Coe (FiniteFrameClass) (FrameClass) := ⟨FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass⟩

abbrev FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass (𝔽 : FrameClass) : FiniteFrameClass := { FF | FF.toFrame ∈ 𝔽 }
postfix:max "ꟳ" => FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass


lemma FrameClass.iff_mem_restrictFinite {𝔽 : FrameClass} {F : Frame} (h : F ∈ 𝔽) [Finite F.World] : ⟨F⟩ ∈ 𝔽ꟳ := by simpa;

section

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊` -/
abbrev AllFrameClass : FrameClass := Set.univ

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓` -/
abbrev ReflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐃` -/
abbrev SerialFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Serial F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝟒` -/
abbrev TransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝟓` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/
abbrev ReflexiveEuclideanFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Euclidean F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝐁` -/
abbrev ReflexiveSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Symmetric F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐒𝟓` -/
abbrev UniversalFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Universal F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊.𝟑` -/
abbrev ConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐈𝐧𝐭` and `𝐒𝟒` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F }
alias PreorderFrameClass := ReflexiveTransitiveFrameClass

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐂` and `𝐒𝟒.𝟐` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveConfluentFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Confluent F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐋𝐂` and `𝐒𝟒.𝟑` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveConnectedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Connected F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐂𝐥` and `𝐊𝐓𝟒𝐁` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F ∧ Transitive F ∧ Symmetric F }
alias EquivalenceFrameClass := ReflexiveTransitiveSymmetricFrameClass

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐋` -/
abbrev TransitiveConverseWellFoundedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F ∧ ConverseWellFounded F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐋` (Finite version) -/
abbrev TransitiveIrreflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F ∧ Irreflexive F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐫𝐳` -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveWeaklyConverseWellFoundedFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Transitive F ∧ WeaklyConverseWellFounded F }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐆𝐫𝐳` (Finite version) -/
abbrev ReflexiveTransitiveAntiSymmetricFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel ∧ Transitive F ∧ AntiSymmetric F }

end

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Logic.System
import Foundation.Vorspiel.BinaryRelations
import Foundation.Vorspiel.RelItr

/-
  DEPRECATED!!
-/

universe u v
-- set_option autoImplicit false

namespace LO.Kripke

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

instance : CoeSort Frame (Type u) := ⟨Frame.World⟩
instance : CoeFun Frame (λ F => F.World → F.World → Prop) := ⟨Frame.Rel⟩

instance {F : Frame} : Nonempty F.World := F.World_nonempty

abbrev Frame.Rel' {F : Frame} (x y : F.World) := F.Rel x y
infix:45 " ≺ " => Frame.Rel'

protected abbrev Frame.RelItr' {F : Frame} (n : ℕ) := F.Rel.iterate n
notation x:45 " ≺^[" n "] " y:46 => Frame.RelItr' n x y


noncomputable abbrev Frame.default {F : Frame} : F.World := Classical.choice F.World_nonempty
notation "﹫" => Frame.default


set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev Frame.Dep (α : Type v) := Frame.{u}

abbrev Frame.alt (F : Frame.{u}) (α : Type v) : Frame.Dep α := F
notation F:max "#" α:max => Frame.alt F α


structure FiniteFrame extends Frame where
  [World_finite : Finite World]

instance {F : FiniteFrame} : Finite (F.World) := F.World_finite
instance : Coe (FiniteFrame) (Frame) := ⟨λ F ↦ F.toFrame⟩


abbrev FrameClass := Set (Frame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FrameClass.{u}

abbrev FrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FrameClass) (α : Type v) : FrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽

notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FiniteFrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) : FrameClass := 𝔽.image FiniteFrame.toFrame
-- instance : Coe (FiniteFrameClass) (FrameClass) := ⟨FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass⟩

abbrev FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass (𝔽 : FrameClass) : FiniteFrameClass := { FF | FF.toFrame ∈ 𝔽 }
postfix:max "ꟳ" => FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass


lemma FrameClass.iff_mem_restrictFinite {𝔽 : FrameClass} {F : Frame} (h : F ∈ 𝔽) [Finite F.World] : ⟨F⟩ ∈ 𝔽ꟳ := by simpa;

section

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊` -/
abbrev AllFrameClass : FrameClass := Set.univ

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓` -/
abbrev ReflexiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Reflexive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐃` -/
abbrev SerialFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Serial F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝟒` -/
abbrev TransitiveFrameClass : FrameClass := { F | Transitive F.Rel }

/-- FrameClass for `𝐊𝐓𝟓` (`𝐒𝟓`) -/

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

namespace LO.Kripke

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

instance : CoeSort Frame (Type u) := ⟨Frame.World⟩
instance : CoeFun Frame (λ F => F.World → F.World → Prop) := ⟨Frame.Rel⟩

instance {F : Frame} : Nonempty F.World := F.World_nonempty

abbrev Frame.Rel' {F : Frame} (x y : F.World) := F.Rel x y

3. **Conclusion**: Since "x ≺ y" simplifies directly to false under the given lemma, we have proven that for any x and y in PointFrame.World, the relation "x ≺ y" does not hold.

informal_statement: There exists a frame with exactly one node such that every node satisfies exactly one successor.
informal_proof:
First, we define a frame with a single node, here represented as the unit type, which contains a single element, typically denoted as ∗.

Given that the frame has exactly one node, and considering the accessibility relation (Rel) defined for the frame as always returning false, we observe that each node has no successors since the accessibility relation is null.

However, the claim is that every node has exactly one successor. This implies that in contradiction to the defined accessibility relation, we must conclude that no such frame with the required properties exists.

Therefore, the statement is false based on the provided formalization.

C1_dependencies.name: Set.univ
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- The universal set on a type `α` is the set containing all elements of `α`.

This is conceptually the "same as" `α` (in set theory, it is actually the same), but type theory

informal_proof:
To establish this statement, we proceed by induction on \( n \).

**Base Case (\( n = 0 \)):**
For \( n = 0 \), the relation \( x \preceq^{0} y \) simplifies to \( x = y \). By definition, this holds true only when \( x \) and \( y \) are the same. Therefore, the base case is satisfied.

**Inductive Step:**
Assume that for some \( n \), the statement holds: \( x \preceq^{n} y \) implies \( x = y \). We need to show that \( x \preceq^{n+1} y \) also implies \( x = y \).

Given \( x \preceq^{n+1} y \), by the definition of \( \preceq^{n+1} \), it follows that \( x \preceq^{n} y \) and \( x \preceq y \). By the inductive hypothesis, \( x \preceq^{n} y \) implies \( x = y \). Thus, \( x = y \) must hold, satisfying the inductive step.

Therefore, by induction, the statement holds for all \( n \).

informal_statement: For all propositions \( a \) and \( b \), \( a \land b \) is equivalent to \( b \land a \), demonstrating the commutative property of logical conjunction.
informal_proof:
We begin by recognizing that the logical "and" operator is commutative. This means that the order in which the propositions are presented in a conjunction does not affect its truth value.

To establish this equivalence formally, we consider two cases: when both \( a \) and \( b \) are true, and when at least one of them is false.

1. **Case 1: Both \( a \) and \( b \) are true.**
   - In this scenario, \( a \land b \) evaluates to true.
   - Similarly, \( b \land a \) also evaluates to true since both \( a \) and \( b \) are true.
   - Thus, \( a \land b \) and \( b \land a \) share the same truth value.

2. **Case 2: At least one of \( a \) or \( b \) is false.**
   - If \( a \) is false, then \( b \land a \) becomes \( b \land \) false, which is false.
   - Similarly, if \( b \) is false, \( a \land b \) becomes false.
   - Therefore, in both subcases, \( a \land b \) and \( b \land a \) evaluate to the same truth value.

Since both cases result in \( a \land b \) and \( b \land a \) having identical truth values, we conclude that \( a \land b \) is equivalent to \( b \land a \), thereby proving the commutativity of logical conjunction.

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

instance : CoeSort Frame (Type u) := ⟨Frame.World⟩
instance : CoeFun Frame (λ F => F.World → F.World → Prop) := ⟨Frame.Rel⟩

instance {F : Frame} : Nonempty F.World := F.World_nonempty

abbrev Frame.Rel' {F : Frame} (x y : F.World) := F.Rel x y
infix:45 " ≺ " => Frame.Rel'

protected abbrev Frame.RelItr' {F : Frame} (n : ℕ) := F.Rel.iterate n
notation x:45 " ≺^[" n "] " y:46 => Frame.RelItr' n x y


noncomputable abbrev Frame.default {F : Frame} : F.World := Classical.choice F.World_nonempty
notation "﹫" => Frame.default


set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev Frame.Dep (α : Type v) := Frame.{u}

abbrev Frame.alt (F : Frame.{u}) (α : Type v) : Frame.Dep α := F

structure FiniteFrame extends Frame where
  [World_finite : Finite World]

instance {F : FiniteFrame} : Finite (F.World) := F.World_finite
instance : Coe (FiniteFrame) (Frame) := ⟨λ F ↦ F.toFrame⟩


abbrev FrameClass := Set (Frame)

abbrev FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) : FrameClass := 𝔽.image FiniteFrame.toFrame
-- instance : Coe (FiniteFrameClass) (FrameClass) := ⟨FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass⟩

import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Logic.System
import Foundation.Vorspiel.BinaryRelations
import Foundation.Vorspiel.RelItr

/-
  DEPRECATED!!
-/

universe u v
-- set_option autoImplicit false

namespace LO.Kripke

structure Frame where
  World : Type u
  Rel : Rel World World
  [World_nonempty : Nonempty World]

instance : CoeSort Frame (Type u) := ⟨Frame.World⟩
instance : CoeFun Frame (λ F => F.World → F.World → Prop) := ⟨Frame.Rel⟩

instance {F : Frame} : Nonempty F.World := F.World_nonempty

abbrev Frame.Rel' {F : Frame} (x y : F.World) := F.Rel x y
infix:45 " ≺ " => Frame.Rel'

protected abbrev Frame.RelItr' {F : Frame} (n : ℕ) := F.Rel.iterate n
notation x:45 " ≺^[" n "] " y:46 => Frame.RelItr' n x y


noncomputable abbrev Frame.default {F : Frame} : F.World := Classical.choice F.World_nonempty
notation "﹫" => Frame.default


set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev Frame.Dep (α : Type v) := Frame.{u}

abbrev Frame.alt (F : Frame.{u}) (α : Type v) : Frame.Dep α := F
notation F:max "#" α:max => Frame.alt F α


structure FiniteFrame extends Frame where
  [World_finite : Finite World]

instance {F : FiniteFrame} : Finite (F.World) := F.World_finite
instance : Coe (FiniteFrame) (Frame) := ⟨λ F ↦ F.toFrame⟩


abbrev FrameClass := Set (Frame)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev FrameClass.Dep (α : Type v) := FrameClass.{u}

abbrev FrameClass.alt (𝔽 : FrameClass) (α : Type v) : FrameClass.Dep.{u} α := 𝔽
notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass := Set (FiniteFrame)

notation:max 𝔽:max "#" α:max => FiniteFrameClass.alt 𝔽 α


abbrev FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass (𝔽 : FiniteFrameClass) : FrameClass := 𝔽.image FiniteFrame.toFrame
-- instance : Coe (FiniteFrameClass) (FrameClass) := ⟨FiniteFrameClass.toFrameClass⟩

abbrev FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass (𝔽 : FrameClass) : FiniteFrameClass := { FF | FF.toFrame ∈ 𝔽 }
postfix:max "ꟳ" => FrameClass.toFiniteFrameClass

informal_statement: A ClassicalValuation assigns to each element of a type α a truth value, either true or false.
informal_proof:
To understand what a ClassicalValuation is, we first need to unpack its definition:

```lean4
abbrev ClassicalValuation (α : Type*) := α → Prop
```

This declaration defines a label `ClassicalValuation` which is a function that takes a type `α` and returns a `Prop`. In Lean4, `Prop` represents the type of propositions, which are statements that can be either true or false. 

Informally, we can think of `ClassicalValuation` as a mechanism to assign a truth value to each element of type `α`. Specifically, for any given `α`, `ClassicalValuation` provides a way to map elements of `α` to propositions, and thus to truth values (true or false). This aligns with the classical notion of a function that assigns a boolean value to each element of a set or type.

In mathematical terms, if `α` is a set, then a ClassicalValuation can be seen as a subset of `α`, where each element in the subset is assigned the truth value true, and each element not in the subset is assigned the truth value false. This interpretation aligns with the classical understanding of sets in mathematics as collections of well-defined objects.

Furthermore, in the context of formal proofs, ClassicalValuation serves as a foundational concept for constructing predicates and propositions. By assigning truth values to elements, we can build logical statements and proofs that depend on these truth assignments. This is particularly useful in areas such as logic, set theory, and formal verification, where precise assignments of truth values are essential for rigorous reasoning.

In summary, a ClassicalValuation is a function that assigns truth values to elements of a type, providing a systematic way to work with propositions in a classical logical framework.

import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Logic.System
import Foundation.Vorspiel.BinaryRelations
import Foundation.Vorspiel.RelItr

/-
  DEPRECATED!!
